text:
m1 - CORRECTION TO MY OWN RECOMMENDATION on the zero-support boundary, recorded here because the bead is where someone will price it.

I said exclusion was cheap because CostBreakdown already has an exclusion field. THE FIELD EXISTS; THE VALUE DOES NOT. Exclusion is a single-case enum - Unreachable, "the candidate reference is not a node of the view" (cost.scala:160-162). That is a claim about the REFERENCE. Zero support is a claim about the EVIDENCE: the node is in the view and nothing weighted was measured about it. Reusing Unreachable would be the same kind of lie this candidate removes.

HONEST COST: a new Exclusion case, its wire handling, its codec enum decoder (align.scala:222), and a further golden re-cut - on top of the hsmm/v1 schema decision already outstanding.

WHAT MAKES IT WORTH IT ANYWAY: the mechanism already works. hsmm.scala:587 builds the state space with `collect { case (s, b) if !b.excluded => s }`, so an excluded cell is DROPPED rather than priced and never competes with external. HsmmResult.validated:410 refuses an admitted state carrying an excluded record, enforcing the invariant from the other side. Only the vocabulary is missing.

AND THE PRECEDENT UNDERCUTS MY EARLIER OBJECTION. I rejected "clamp to a large constant" as arbitrary, but CostBreakdown.unreachable at :256 pairs Exclusion.Unreachable with Double.MaxValue/4. The codebase's existing answer to "cannot assess" is exclusion PLUS a sentinel, so a second case would follow the pattern rather than invent one.

ALTERNATIVE, narrower and insufficient on its own: reject zero-weight-sum configurations at CostWeights.of. Nonzero chart weight with zero dense weights still leaves a chartless cell at zero present weight, so the hole survives.

Nothing built. The [0,1] guard widening remains in the branch as correct-on-its-own; the boundary policy is the chief's.
